# createStyle

A zero-dependency React utility (~1kb minified, ~500b gzipped) that creates reusable styled components from CSS class strings. Designed for Tailwind CSS but works with any class-based styling system. Think `styled-components` but class-based, not CSS-in-JS.

## Install

```
npm install @josephmark/createstyle
```

## Signature

```ts
createStyle<T = ElementType>(
  defaultTag: React.ElementType,
  classes?: string,
  defaultProps?: { displayName?: string } & AllHTMLAttributes<T>
): CustomTag<T>
```

Returns a `CustomTag<T>`: a `forwardRef` React component with extra properties:
- `.classNames: string` — the pre-set class string passed at creation time
- `.props` — the default props passed at creation time
- `.toString()` — returns `.classNames`, enabling `className={MyTag}` usage

Classes passed at render time via `className` are **appended** to the pre-set classes, never replaced.

## Basic usage

```tsx
import createStyle from "@josephmark/createstyle"

const H1 = createStyle("h1", "text-lg font-serif leading-[1.5]")
const P  = createStyle("p",  "tracking-wide")

const Header = () => (
  <header>
    <H1 className="mb-5">Hello</H1>
    <P>World</P>
  </header>
)
```

## Key patterns

### Override tag at render time (`as` prop)

`as` accepts an intrinsic tag name or any React component.

```tsx
const H3 = createStyle("h3", "text-lg tracking-wide")
<H3 as="h1">Semantically an h1, styled as h3</H3>
```

### Render as a React component

The merged class string is passed to the component as `className`, so the component
must accept and apply `className`.

```tsx
import Link from "next/link"
const Button = createStyle("button", "rounded-full bg-red-500 px-4 py-2")
<Button as={Link} href="/signup">Sign up</Button>
```

A component can also be the default tag:

```tsx
const StyledLink = createStyle(Link, "underline underline-offset-2")
<StyledLink href="/about">About</StyledLink>
```

Limitation: render-time props are typed as `AllHTMLAttributes`, so props on the target
component that aren't HTML attributes are a type error (`href` is fine; react-router's
`to` is not). Wrap the component or cast in that case.

### Generic for correct ref and prop types
```ts
const Button = createStyle<HTMLButtonElement>("button", "rounded bg-red-500 text-white")
```

### Default props (e.g. input type)
```ts
const Checkbox = createStyle("input", "rounded border", { type: "checkbox" })
```

### Display name for React devtools
```ts
const Card = createStyle("article", "rounded p-2 bg-white shadow-lg", { displayName: "Card" })
```

### Extract class string for use elsewhere
```tsx
const P = createStyle("p", "leading-[1.2] text-[1rem]")
// All three are equivalent:
<div className={P}>...</div>
<div className={P.toString()}>...</div>
<div className={P.classNames}>...</div>
```

### Extract default props
```tsx
const Checkbox = createStyle("input", "rounded", { style: { boxShadow: "0 0 0 4px black" } })
<Checkbox style={{ ...Checkbox.props.style, backgroundColor: "red" }} />
```

### Dynamic classes — works with clsx or any string
```tsx
import clsx from "clsx"
const Btn = createStyle("button", "rounded py-2 px-4", { type: "button" })
<Btn className={clsx(active ? "bg-red-500" : "bg-blue-500")}>Click</Btn>
```

### Themed components
```tsx
const THEMES = {
  serif: createStyle("h2", "font-serif text-lg"),
  sans:  createStyle("h2", "font-sans text-xl tracking-tight"),
}
const ThemableHeading = ({ theme, children }) => {
  const C = THEMES[theme]
  return <C>{children}</C>
}
```

### Forwarded refs
```tsx
const Container = createStyle<HTMLDivElement>("div", "max-w-screen-xl mx-auto")
const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)
<Container ref={ref} />
```

## Types

```ts
/** Props accepted by any createStyle component at render time */
type CustomTagArgs<T = ElementType> = {
  /** Overwrite the rendered tag or component at render time. Accepts an intrinsic
   *  tag name ("h1") or any React component. */
  as?: React.ElementType
  // `as` is omitted from AllHTMLAttributes, which declares its own `as?: string`
  // for `<link rel="preload">`; without the Omit the two intersect down to
  // `React.ElementType & string`, which rejects every component.
} & Omit<AllHTMLAttributes<T>, "as">

/** The component type returned by createStyle — a forwardRef component with extra static properties */
type CustomTag<T = ElementType> = {
  /** The CSS class string set at creation time */
  classNames?: string
  /** The default props set at creation time (excluding displayName) */
  props?: { displayName?: string } & AllHTMLAttributes<T>
} & ForwardRefExoticComponent<CustomTagArgs<T> & RefAttributes<T>>
```

## Notes

- `displayName` in `defaultProps` sets `component.displayName` for React devtools and is stripped from rendered DOM props
- Without an explicit `displayName`, the devtools name is `*` plus the tag name, or the component's `displayName`/`name` when the default tag is a component
- Class merge order: `classes` (creation) → `className` from `defaultProps` → `className` from render props
- The package has no runtime dependencies; React is a peer dependency
